ναασσων.def: of Hebrew origin (H5177); Naasson (i.e. Nachshon), an Israelite. KJV: Naasson.

ναγγαι.def: probably of Hebrew origin (compare H5052); Nangæ (i.e. perhaps Nogach), an Israelite. KJV: Nagge.

ναζαρεθ.def: of uncertain derivation; Nazareth or Nazaret, a place in Palestine. KJV: Nazareth.

ναζαρηνοσ.def: from Ναζαρέθ (G3478); a Nazarene, i.e. inhabitant of Nazareth. KJV: of Nazareth.

ναζωραιοσ.def: from Ναζαρέθ (G3478); a Nazoræan, i.e. inhabitant of Nazareth; by extension, a Christian. KJV: Nazarene, of Nazareth.

ναθαν.def: of Hebrew origin (H5416); Nathan, an Israelite. KJV: Nathan.

ναθαναηλ.def: of Hebrew origin (H5417); Nathanaël (i.e. Nathanel), an Israelite and Christian. KJV: Nathanael.

ναι.def: a primary particle of strong affirmation; yes. KJV: even so, surely, truth, verily, yea, yes.

ναιν.def: probably of Hebrew origin (compare H4999); Nain, a place in Palestine. KJV: Nain.

ναοσ.def: from a primary ναίω (to dwell); a fane, shrine, temple. KJV: shrine, temple.

ναουμ.def: of Hebrew origin (H5151); Naum (i.e. Nachum), an Israelite. KJV: Naum.

ναρκισσοσ.def: a flower of the same name, from νάρκη (stupefaction, as a "narcotic"); Narcissus, a Roman. KJV: Narcissus.

ναυαγεω.def: from a compound of ναῦς (G3491) and ἄγω (G71); to be shipwrecked (stranded, "navigate"), literally or figuratively. KJV: make (suffer) shipwreck.

ναυκληροσ.def: from ναῦς (G3491) and κλῆρος (G2819) ("clerk"); a captain. KJV: owner of a ship.

ναυσ.def: from νάω or νέω (to float); a boat (of any size). KJV: ship.

ναυτησ.def: from ναῦς (G3491); a boatman, i.e. seaman. KJV: sailor, shipman.

ναχωρ.def: of Hebrew origin (H5152); Nachor, the grandfather of Abraham. KJV: Nachor.

νεανιασ.def: from a derivative of νέος (G3501); a youth (up to about forty years). KJV: young man.

νεανισκοσ.def: from the same as νεανίας (G3494); a youth (under forty). KJV: young man.

νεαπολισ.def: from νέος (G3501) and πόλις (G4172); new town; Neapolis, a place in Macedonia. KJV: Neapolis.

νεεμαν.def: of Hebrew origin (H5283); Neeman (i.e. Naaman), a Syrian. KJV: Naaman.

νεκροσ.def: from an apparently primary νέκυς (a corpse); dead (literally or figuratively; also as noun). KJV: dead.

νεκροω.def: from νεκρός (G3498); to deaden, i.e. (figuratively) to subdue. KJV: be dead, mortify.

νεκρωσισ.def: from νεκρόω (G3499); decease; figuratively, impotency. KJV: deadness, dying.

νεοσ.def: including the comparative νεότερος; a primary word; "new", i.e. (of persons) youthful, or (of things) fresh; figuratively, regenerate. KJV: new, young.

νεοσσοσ.def: from νέος (G3501); a youngling (nestling). KJV: young.

νεοτησ.def: from νέος (G3501); newness, i.e. youthfulness. KJV: youth.

νεοφυτοσ.def: from νέος (G3501) and a derivative of φύω (G5453); newly planted, i.e. (figuratively) a young convert ("neophyte"). KJV: novice.

νερων.def: of Latin origin; Neron (i.e. Nero), a Roman emperor. KJV: Nero.

νευω.def: apparently a primary verb; to "nod", i.e. (by analogy), signal. KJV: beckon.

νεφελη.def: from νέφος (G3509); properly, cloudiness, i.e. (concretely) a cloud. KJV: cloud.

νεφθαλειμ.def: of Hebrew origin (H5321); Nephthaleim (i.e. Naphthali), a tribe in Palestine. KJV: Nephthalim.

νεφοσ.def: apparently a primary word; a cloud. KJV: cloud.

νεφροσ.def: of uncertain affinity; a kidney (plural), i.e. (figuratively) the inmost mind. KJV: reins.

νεωκοροσ.def: from a form of ναός (G3485) and κορέω (to sweep); a temple-servant, i.e. (by implication) a votary. KJV: worshipper.

νεωτερικοσ.def: from the comparative of νέος (G3501); appertaining to younger persons, i.e. juvenile. KJV: youthful.

νη.def: probably an intensive form of ναί (G3483); a particle of attestation (accompanied by the object invoked or appealed to in confirmation); as sure as. KJV: I protest by.

νηθω.def: from νέω (of like meaning); to spin. KJV: spin.

νηπιαζω.def: from νήπιος (G3516); to act as a babe, i.e. (figuratively) innocently. KJV: be a child.

νηπιοσ.def: from an obsolete particle νή- (implying negation) and ἔπος (G2031); not speaking, i.e. an infant (minor); figuratively, a simple-minded person, an immature Christian. KJV: babe, child (+ -ish).

νηρευσ.def: apparently from a derivative of the base of ναῦς (G3491) (meaning wet); Nereus, a Christian. KJV: Nereus.

νηρι.def: of Hebrew origin (H5374); Neri (i.e. Nerijah), an Israelite. KJV: Neri.

νησιον.def: diminutive of νῆσος (G3520); an islet. KJV: island.

νησοσ.def: probably from the base of ναῦς (G3491); an island. KJV: island, isle.

νηστεια.def: from νηστεύω (G3522); abstinence (from lack of food, or voluntary and religious); specially, the fast of the Day of Atonement. KJV: fast(-ing).

νηστευω.def: from νῆστις (G3523); to abstain from food (religiously). KJV: fast.

νηστισ.def: from the inseparable negative particle νή- (not) and ἐσθίω (G2068); not eating, i.e. abstinent from food (religiously). KJV: fasting.

νηφαλεοσ.def: from νήφω (G3525); sober, i.e. (figuratively) circumspect. KJV: sober.

νηφω.def: of uncertain affinity; to abstain from wine (keep sober), i.e. (figuratively) be discreet. KJV: be sober, watch.

νιγερ.def: of Latin origin; black; Niger, a Christian. KJV: Niger.

νικανωρ.def: probably from νικάω (G3528); victorious; Nicanor, a Christian. KJV: Nicanor.

νικαω.def: from νίκη (G3529); to subdue (literally or figuratively). KJV: conquer, overcome, prevail, get the victory.

νικη.def: apparently a primary word; conquest (abstractly), i.e. (figuratively) the means of success. KJV: victory.

νικοδημοσ.def: from νῖκος (G3534) and δῆμος (G1218); victorious among his people; Nicodemus, an Israelite. KJV: Nicodemus.

νικολαιτησ.def: from Νικόλαος (G3532); a Nicolaite, i.e. adherent of Nicolaus. KJV: Nicolaitane.

νικολαοσ.def: from νῖκος (G3534) and Λαοδικεύς (G2994); victorious over the people; Nicolaus, a heretic. KJV: Nicolaus.

νικοπολισ.def: from νῖκος (G3534) and πόλις (G4172); victorious city; Nicopolis, a place in Macedonia. KJV: Nicopolis.

νικοσ.def: from νίκη (G3529); a conquest (concretely), i.e. (by implication) triumph. KJV: victory.

νινευι.def: of Hebrew origin (H5210); Ninevi (i.e. Nineveh), the capital of Assyria. KJV: Nineve.

νινευιτησ.def: from Νινευΐ (G3535); a Ninevite, i.e. inhabitant of Nineveh. KJV: of Nineve, Ninevite.

νιπτηρ.def: from νίπτω (G3538); a ewer. KJV: bason.

νιπτω.def: to cleanse (especially the hands or the feet or the face); ceremonially, to perform ablution. KJV: wash.

νοημα.def: from νοιέω (G3539); a perception, i.e. purpose, or (by implication) the intellect, disposition, itself. KJV: device, mind, thought.

νοθοσ.def: of uncertain affinity; a spurious or illegitimate son. KJV: bastard.

νοιεω.def: from νοῦς (G3563); to exercise the mind (observe), i.e. (figuratively) to comprehend, heed. KJV: consider, perceive, think, understand.

νομη.def: feminine from the same as νόμος (G3551); pasture, i.e. (the act) feeding (figuratively, spreading of a gangrene), or (the food) pasturage. KJV: X eat, pasture.

νομιζω.def: from νόμος (G3551); properly, to do by law (usage), i.e. to accustom (passively, be usual); by extension, to deem or regard. KJV: suppose, thing, be wont.

νομικοσ.def: from νόμος (G3551); according (or pertaining) to law, i.e. legal (ceremonially); as noun, an expert in the (Mosaic) law. KJV: about the law, lawyer.

νομιμωσ.def: adverb from a derivative of νόμος (G3551); legitimately (specially, agreeably to the rules of the lists). KJV: lawfully.

νομισμα.def: from νομίζω (G3543); what is reckoned as of value (after the Latin numisma), i.e. current coin. KJV: money.

νομοδιδασκαλοσ.def: from νόμος (G3551) and διδάσκαλος (G1320); an expounder of the (Jewish) law, i.e. a Rabbi. KJV: doctor (teacher) of the law.

νομοθεσια.def: from νομοθέτης (G3550); legislation (specially, the institution of the Mosaic code). KJV: giving of the law.

νομοθετεω.def: from νομοθέτης (G3550); to legislate, i.e. (passively) to have (the Mosaic) enactments injoined, be sanctioned (by them). KJV: establish, receive the law.

νομοθετησ.def: from νόμος (G3551) and a derivative of τίθημι (G5087); a legislator. KJV: lawgiver.

νομοσ.def: from a primary νέμω (to parcel out, especially food or grazing to animals); law (through the idea of prescriptive usage), genitive case (regulation), specially, (of Moses (including the volume); also of the Gospel), or figuratively (a principle). KJV: law.

νοσεω.def: from νόσος (G3554); to be sick, i.e. (by implication, of a diseased appetite) to hanker after (figuratively, to harp upon). KJV: dote.

νοσημα.def: from νοσέω (G3552); an ailment. KJV: disease.

νοσοσ.def: of uncertain affinity; a malady (rarely figuratively, of moral disability). KJV: disease, infirmity, sickness.

νοσσια.def: from νεοσσός (G3502); a brood (of chickens). KJV: brood.

νοσσιον.def: diminutive of νεοσσός (G3502); a birdling. KJV: chicken.

νοσφιζομαι.def: middle voice from νοσφί (apart or clandestinely); to sequestrate for oneself, i.e. embezzle. KJV: keep back, purloin.

νοτοσ.def: of uncertain affinity; the south(-west) wind; by extension, the southern quarter itself. KJV: south (wind).

νουθεσια.def: from νοῦς (G3563) and a derivative of τίθημι (G5087); calling attention to, i.e. (by implication) mild rebuke or warning. KJV: admonition.

νουθετεω.def: from the same as νουθεσία (G3559); to put in mind, i.e. (by implication) to caution or reprove gently. KJV: admonish, warn.

νουμηνια.def: feminine of a compound of νέος (G3501) and μήν (G3376) (as noun by implication, of ἡμέρα (G2250)); the festival of new moon. KJV: new moon.

νουνεχωσ.def: adverb from a comparative of the accusative case of νοῦς (G3563) and ἔχω (G2192); in a mind-having way, i.e. prudently. KJV: discreetly.

νουσ.def: probably from the base of γινώσκω (G1097); the intellect, i.e. mind (divine or human; in thought, feeling, or will); by implication, meaning. KJV: mind, understanding.

νυμφασ.def: probably contracted for a compound of νύμφη (G3565) and δῶρον (G1435); nymph-given (i.e. -born); Nymphas, a Christian. KJV: Nymphas.

νυμφη.def: from a primary but obsolete verb νύπτω (to veil as a bride; compare Latin "nupto," to marry); a young married woman (as veiled), including a betrothed girl; by implication, a son's wife. KJV: bride, daughter in law.

νυμφιοσ.def: from νύμφη (G3565); a bride-groom (literally or figuratively). KJV: bridegroom.

νυμφων.def: from νύμφη (G3565); the bridal room. KJV: bridechamber.

νυν.def: a primary particle of present time; "now" (as adverb of date, a transition or emphasis); also as noun or adjective present or immediate. KJV: henceforth, + hereafter, of late, soon, present, this (time).

νυνι.def: a prolonged form of νῦν (G3568) for emphasis; just now. KJV: now.

νυξ.def: a primary word; "night" (literally or figuratively). KJV: (mid-)night.

νυσσω.def: apparently a primary word; to prick ("nudge"). KJV: pierce.

νυσταζω.def: from a presumed derivative of νεύω (G3506); to nod, i.e. (by implication) to fall asleep; figuratively, to delay. KJV: slumber.

νυχθημερον.def: from νύξ (G3571) and ἡμέρα (G2250); a day-and-night, i.e. full day of twenty-four hours. KJV: night and day.

νωε.def: of Hebrew origin (H5146); Noë, (i.e. Noäch), a patriarch. KJV: Noe.

νωθροσ.def: from a derivative of νόθος (G3541); sluggish, i.e. (literally) lazy, or (figuratively) stupid. KJV: dull, slothful.

νωτοσ.def: of uncertain affinity; the back. KJV: back.
